prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: مواقيت الصلاة في مدن سعودية (language ar, right-to-left: column 1 is on the RIGHT).
Grid: 6 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "المدينة" · longest unbreakable word 49px · one-line width 91px
  col 2: header "الفجر" · longest unbreakable word 35px · one-line width 35px
  col 3: header "الظهر" · longest unbreakable word 35px · one-line width 35px
  col 4: header "العصر" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 38px
  col 5: header "المغرب" · longest unbreakable word 47px · one-line width 47px
  col 6: header "العشاء" · longest unbreakable word 41px · one-line width 41px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"A quick-reference prayer-time table for Saudi cities: one city per row, with five daily prayer times to compare across cities and across prayers.","reading":"Right-to-left: the reader finds the city in the rightmost column, then scans leftward across the five prayer-time columns; vertical scanning compares the same prayer across cities, so the five time columns need a consistent rhythm.","groups":["Column 1 is the row identifier and should be visually separate from the data.","Columns 2–6 form one parallel group of prayer times; they share the same value type and should read as a coherent block, with الفجر/الظهر/العصر as the daytime run and المغرب/العشاء as the evening pair."],"keep_intact":["HH:MM time values must never split across lines.","City names should ideally stay on one line; if not, they must wrap only at spaces between words.","Arabic header words should not be broken mid-word if avoidable."],"may_wrap":["Long city names such as المدينة المنورة and مكة المكرمة at word spaces.","Longer prayer headers such as المغرب and العشاء if the column budget is tight; row height can absorb a second header line."]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r2A: widths [70, 56, 56, 59, 68, 62] · table 372×301px · row heights [36, 36, 60, 60, 36, 36, 36] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 12px
Design r2B: widths [72, 58, 58, 60, 49, 62] · table 360×325px · row heights [60, 36, 60, 60, 36, 36, 36] · column headers wrapped 1/6 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2C: widths [72, 56, 56, 59, 68, 48] · table 360×348px · row heights [60, 36, 60, 60, 60, 36, 36] · column headers wrapped 1/6 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 2

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}

log.raw: {"critique":[{"design":"r2A","good":"Every column header sits on one line, every HH:MM value sits on one line, city names wrap only at their word spaces, and the 68/62px evening pair (المغرب/العشاء) reads with the same weight as the daytime run. Rows 2–3 grow to 60px only because of the city names, which is the right reason.","problems":"The table is 372px wide and overflows the 360px box by 12px: the leftmost column (العشاء, the last prayer of the day) is cut off at the box edge, so its times can only be read by scrolling horizontally. Functionally the most important edge of the table is the one that is clipped.","cause":"Each column is already at its hard minimum — the wider of header word and time value plus 21px padding (70 for المدينة, 56 الفجر, 56 الظهر, 59 العصر, 68 المغرب, 62 العشاء). That minimum set sums to 371, so the 12px cannot be recovered from any column without splitting either a header word or a time value."},{"design":"r2B","good":"Fits the box exactly (360px), keeps every time value intact and on one line, wraps city names only at spaces, and the header row is uniform in height so the columns still read as one parallel block.","problems":"المغرب is broken mid-word into «المغ» / «رب» across two lines, so one column header is visibly torn while العشاء next to it stays on one line; the evening pair therefore loses its symmetry and the reader's eye catches the break before the data.","cause":"To buy the missing 12px, المغرب was cut from 68 to 49px, leaving 28px of text width against a 47px word. The reclaimed space went into المدينة (72) and العصر/الظهر (60/58), which did not need it."},{"design":"r2C","good":"Fits the box, gives the city column the most room (72px) so city names break at clean word boundaries, and keeps الظهر/المغرب generous.","problems":"Two mid-word splits: the العشاء header becomes «الع» / «شاء», and — far worse — the العشاء time values themselves break («٨:٢» / «٣»). Numbers that split across lines are unreadable as times, and the damage makes rows 2, 4 and 5 grow to 60px so the row rhythm turns ragged (60, 36, 60, 60, 60, 36, 36).","cause":"العشاء was squeezed to 48px, i.e. 27px of text for a 41px header and a ~30px value — below both thresholds. The 20px released there was spent widening المغرب to 68 and الظهر to 59, which were already comfortable."}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"maghrib-wrap-359","widths":[70,56,56,59,56,62],"change":"Keep the city column and all four other time columns at their exact minimum (so المدينة, الفجر, الظهر, العصر, العشاء headers and every HH:MM value stay on one line, cities wrapping only at spaces), and take the whole 12px deficit out of المغرب alone (68→56). Result: 359px, no horizontal scroll, no clipped column, and exactly one two-line header — a single header cell pays the cost instead of a whole clipped column or a split number. Accepted trade-off: «المغرب» breaks across two lines, which is the least damaging compromise available at 359px."},{"name":"no-split-371","widths":[70,56,56,59,68,62],"change":"Deliberately return the full minimum set and let the table run 12px past the box. This is the only configuration in which nothing is damaged: all six headers one line, all thirty time values one line, city names broken only at their word spaces. The price is a constant 12px horizontal scroll; if the reader can scroll, this reads better than any 359px layout, because a torn header or a split number is a permanent defect on every row while a 12px scroll is a one-off gesture."},{"name":"scroll-min-369","widths":[70,56,56,59,66,62],"change":"A middle option that tests whether المغرب can be bought back cheaply: trim only 2px from المغرب (68→66) and keep everything else at minimum, giving 369px. It keeps the header on one line (47px word in 45px is still short, so this is a probe rather than a safe design) and reduces the overflow to 9px — use only if the 12px scroll of no-split-371 proves unacceptable in practice; otherwise prefer the clean 371."}]}
